question: How did Jesus respond when questioned by the high priest?
summary: Matthew 26:64 and Luke 22:70 give Jesus the famously evasive 'thou hast said' / 'ye say that I am' — an answer that can be parsed as a yes, a no, or a 'that's your word, not mine.' Mark 14:62 has him answer with no ambiguity at all: *egō eimi*, 'I am.' Same scene, same question, but Mark's Jesus delivers the unconditional self-identification while Matthew and Luke deflect it back onto the questioner.

reconcile.connective: Commentators read Matthew's 'thou hast said' and Luke's 'ye say that I am' as culturally idiomatic affirmatives, substantively equivalent to Mark's direct 'I am.'

discrepancy.connective: Bart Ehrman lists this exact question among his Gospel contradictions, noting Mark's reply is 'a straightforward' affirmation while Luke reworded it for theological reasons.

skeptic.name: Bart D. Ehrman
skeptic.work: Jesus, Interrupted: Revealing the Hidden Contradictions in the Bible (And Why We Don't Know About Them)
skeptic.attribution: Bart D. Ehrman, Jesus, Interrupted (HarperOne, 2009), pp. 50-51

pd_work.resource: John Haley, An Examination of the Alleged Discrepancies of the Bible (1874)
pd_work.author: John Haley
pd_work.note: Haley lists Matt. 26:64 ('Thou hast said') beside Mark 14:62 ('I am') among his catalog of Synoptic 'variant quotations' under the 'Forms of report. Different.' heading (Doctrinal Discrepancies, pp. 153-157), concluding that in every such case 'the fundamental idea is... carefully and distinctly preserved,' so differing wording between the Gospels is no real discrepancy.

excerpts.excerpt_text: This purposefully enigmatic response is essentially an affirmative answer (see 26:25; 27:11); Mark has “I Am” (Mark 14:62).
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: States the tension explicitly (Matthew's reply is 'purposefully enigmatic' where Mark's is the unambiguous 'I Am') and resolves it by reading Matthew's wording as substantively affirmative despite the different form.
excerpts.source_note_text: 26:64 You have said it: This purposefully enigmatic response is essentially an affirmative answer (see 26:25; 27:11); Mark has “I Am” (Mark 14:62). • you will see: By quoting Dan 7:13, Jesus affirmed that he was the Son of Man who would be vindicated and exalted by God. • seated in the place of power at God’s right hand: Literally seated at the right hand of the power; see Ps 110:1. Jews were reluctant to name God directly (see study note on Matt 5:4). • The expression coming on the clouds of heaven could refer either to the destruction of Jerusalem in AD 70 or to Jesus’ second coming at the end of history.
